items.label: text
items.text: Note: Solids should have regularly packed particles touching. Liquids should have most of the particles touching at least some of their neighbours, but with gaps here and there, and no regularity. Gases should have the particles well spaced.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Solids: vibration around a fixed point. Liquids: particles can move around into vacant spaces, but with some difficulty because of the relatively close packing.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Evaporation: Some faster moving particles break away from the surface of the liquid. Boiling: Attractive forces are broken throughout the liquid to produce bubbles of vapour.

items.label: list_item
items.text: D – because it has a lower boiling point the forces of attraction between particles will be weaker therefore it will also evaporate more easily than substance B (the only other substance that is a liquid at 25 °C).

The ring will also take slightly longer to form because of the slower moving particles.
